1 Relativism

Terms change their meanings as the time goes. Modern US conservatism was liberalism of 18th century. Political chart of 18th century would have same words on it but with different meanings. Conservatism in one country is different from conservatism in another.

Political charts are interpreted by those who is in power now. An unfamous term extremism is extremely popular among politicians. John may be extreme right for one politician and centrist for another. Politician can change his stance at any moment making John suddenly 'become extremist' even if his views did not change. Or they may eliminate extremists so current centrists become new extremists.

2 Fluid Language

Politicians change the meanings of the words to their liking. They may claim that only they know what <term> really means, or simply usurp the words. For example, in Russia there is Liberal Democratic Party which in fact is a bunch of monarchists.

More abstract example, imagine there is Left Wingnut party. As the time goes its members are gradually replaced for various reasons. Is it still 'left' party when 30% of members are not 'left'? 50%? Will they admit that they switched polarity? Will they change the brand name?

3 Overgeneralization

Heterogenous aspects of life are grouped under umbrella terms. Church, abortion, banks, unions, welfare, corporations, education, parenting all lumped together and cut into few subscription plans neither of which fits anybody. Can conservative be against church? Can libertarian be against open borders? Can ancap be against non-agression principle? I guess so. But such character will probably not fit onto the chart. In such case typical advice is to pick another chart with other scales. No thanks.

4 Missing Important Details

Political chatter, or 'discourse' as they like to call it to show their importance, may be affected by unaccounted factors. Politician has fundamental conflict of interests because his income depends on what he says. He is vulnerable to blackmailing. He may secretly have other allegiance.

Is corrupt and blackmailed Liberal Right Wingnut party still 'right'? is it still 'liberal'? One may say that the chart is an abstract model where such details are not necessary. I don't think so, because criminal-ruled parties tend to be labeled centrist whereas they should be much closer to totalitarian side.

Conclusion.

Political square/cubic charts are for the people with square/cubic mentality. They do not reflect reality even remotedly. Taking political charts and approved terminology seriously is framing. It is like playing with politicians on their field by their rules.
